segments.text: This panel discusses the ethics of deploying AI systems at scale.
The first panelist argues that transparency must come before automation.
She says users deserve to know when a decision was made by a model.
The second panelist focuses on bias in training data.
He notes that biased data produces biased outcomes at scale.
Auditing datasets before training is his top recommendation.
A third panelist raises the question of accountability when models fail.
She argues a human must remain responsible for high stakes decisions.
The panel agrees that consent for data use is often unclear to users.
They debate whether regulation should be global or regional.
One panelist warns that heavy regulation could slow beneficial research.
Another counters that unregulated deployment risks public trust.
They close by agreeing that clear accountability builds long term trust.
